names.note: Read out of doxologia.ro's line for 19 aprilie, «Sfântul Cuvios Ioan de la Lavra Veche».
Read out of saint.gr's line for 20 Απριλίου, «Όσιος Ιωάννης ο Παλαιολαυρίτης», with the rank word and the epithet left off.

Read out of the Ohrid Prologue's first heading for the Julian 19 April, „Преп. Јован Ветхопешчерник.“, with Преп. left off, which is the `venerable` this folder already carries in `types`. **Ветхопешчерник is kept**: it is not a rank word but the by-name the whole entry turns on — the Old Cave, which is this folder's English name as «of the Old Lavra» — and keeping it is what holds this form out of the seven-folder bare «Јован» fold, on the same reading that kept `Ардалион Глумац` and `Јован Нови Јањински` out of theirs.

The heading of days.pravoslavie.ru’s name page 995, «Иоанн Палеолаврит, Ветхопещерник, иеромонах», with the rank word left off. Both epithets are the calendar’s own and say the same thing twice, the first in Greek and the second in Slavonic: the man of the Old Lavra. The day’s own line declines the second alone, «Прп. Иоанна Ветхопещерника».

source.text: Православный церковный календарь, Сретенский монастырь (days.pravoslavie.ru), 19 апреля ст. ст. — «Прп. Иоанна Ветхопещерника (VIII).»

attestations.note: His name page 995 and his life page both list this one day, which is the day the `romanian` and `serbian` rows already carry; the Greek 20 April is one day off and is unaffected. The day page prints no hymn under his name. The Russian is the first source read for this folder to say where the Old Lavra was and what he was ordained. azbyka.ru was not read.

source.text: Calendarul zilei, Doxologia (doxologia.ro), 19 aprilie — «Sfântul Cuvios Ioan de la Lavra Veche»
saint.gr, το εορτολόγιο της 20ής Απριλίου — «Όσιος Ιωάννης ο Παλαιολαυρίτης»

attestations.note: The life page heads «Τύπος εορτής: Σταθερή. Εορτάζει στις 20 Απριλίου εκάστου έτους», the same day as the listing. **The Greek keeps him a day after the Romanian**, which prints him on 19 aprilie; the folder's Romanian row stands where it is and this row records the day page that was read. The two accounts are plainly one man's: the Greek calls him ο Παλαιολαυρίτης, of the Old Lavra, and says that he was received at the last by the monastery of Chariton, which is that lavra. The Greek adds his childhood — that he kept in his own family all the virtues Scripture enjoins on children, honoured his father and mother, obeyed their wishes and was a pattern of love and mutual help among his brothers — and that he wandered through many places before entering the monastic life and went as a pilgrim to Jerusalem. Under «Ιερά Λείψανα» it puts a portion of his relic at the monastery of the Panagia Tourliani on Mykonos. It gives no year, so no `dates` were taken, and it prints no hymn.

source.text: Православни подсетник (pravoslavno.rs), Охридски пролог за 02.05.2026 (19. април ст. ст.) — „Преп. Јован Ветхопешчерник.“

attestations.note: The day's first entry, on the same menologion day the Romanian keeps him on, where the Greek keeps him on 20 April; one row per church, so the Greek row kept its day and nothing moved. The identification is on the by-name and the place both: Ветхопешчерник is the Old Cave, and the entry's first sentence puts him in the so-called Old Cave, or Lavra of Chariton the Great, in Palestine. **The century is new to this folder**: „Поживе и упокоји се у VIII столећу.“ — he lived and reposed in the eighth century, recorded as the interval a century is. New besides: that he **travelled from his youth about the holy places to hear the teaching and counsel of holy men** before he settled in Chariton's cave, and that there he gave himself to a hard struggle, passing days and years in fasting, prayer and vigil, **thinking unceasingly on death and learning humility**, and was gathered by death like well-ripened fruit. The Prologue prints no troparion and no kontakion.

hymns.text: Cu curgerile lacrimilor tale ai lucrat pustiul cel neroditor şi cu suspinurile cele dintru adânc ai făcut ostenelile tale însutit roditoare; şi te-ai făcut luminător lumii, strălucind cu minunile, Ioan, părintele nostru. Roagă-te lui Hristos Dumnezeu ca să mântuiască sufletele noastre.

source.text: doxologia.ro, «Troparul Sfântului Cuvios Ioan de la Lavra Veche», Glasul 8

english.text: With the streams of your tears you worked the barren desert, and with sighs from the depths you made your labours bear fruit a hundredfold; and you became a light to the world, shining with wonders, John our father. Pray to Christ God that our souls be saved.

death.note: The Ohrid Prologue for 19. април ст. ст.: „Поживе и упокоји се у VIII столећу.“ — he lived and reposed in the eighth century. A century is an interval and is recorded as one, 701 to 800. The folder held no `dates` before: doxologia, which keeps him on this same day, and saint.gr, which keeps him on 20 April, give no year between them. No year of birth is recorded anywhere read.
